page: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v7 is a virtual machine configuration within the Daldsv7 series, featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance operates with dedicated core allocation and clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem is supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16.

The instance includes 472 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, providing direct high-throughput disk access without relying solely on remote volumes. Memory allocation is structured at 2.0 GB per vCPU, representing a compute-heavy 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This density prioritizes core processing speed over memory capacity, omitting GPU accelerators to maximize raw CPU compute and vector calculation efficiency.

Given its lower memory-to-core ratio and rapid local NVMe storage, the D8alds_v7 is structured for compute-focused applications that do not require massive memory working sets. Tradeoffs include limited memory scaling under heavy in-memory operations, offset by fast scratch space and high clock frequency. Appropriate workloads include batch processing, distributed compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, intermediate data transformations, and computational modeling.
description: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating up to 4.5 GHz. The system provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 multithreaded physical cores, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory and 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU package incorporates advanced vector capabilities including AVX-512 and bfloat16 instructions, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread, the configuration favors processing throughput over extensive memory buffers. It includes no dedicated GPUs. The instance is suited for compute-intensive tasks, CI/CD build agents, algorithmic batch execution, and storage-adjacent pipeline processing.
